annotations.text:
A — BLACK LEDGER
The archive. One plate, then work as a ruled index: year, client, scope, medium. Closest to your current site's restraint, and it reads as a practice with a back catalogue rather than a feed.

Tradeoff: the artwork is undersold above the fold. A band scanning for a look sees typography first.

B — GATEFOLD WALL
The poster wall. Twelve plates edge to edge with no margins, condensed display type and one oxblood accent. You see the range in two seconds; the third tile shows the hover state.

Tradeoff: loud, and the pieces compete with each other. Weak work has nowhere to hide in a dense grid.

C — PLATE
One piece at a time, set like liner notes: spec table, process crops, registration marks. Sells the craft and the print thinking to labels and art directors.

Tradeoff: slow to browse and it needs good scans of every stage — the most work to keep fed.
